children: Enterprise software and cloud infrastructure company Oracle Corp. (ORCL, Financials) is set to report earnings with options traders looking for a big move.
The corporation reports fiscal first-quarter data Thursday after the close of the market. Shares closed Tuesday at $162.52, up 2.4%. Options activity indicates traders don't expect a quiet reaction.

Call purchasing has driven the bullish bias with special focus on the $175 strike. That would be nearly an 8% premium to Tuesday's closing price for Oracle. The enthusiasm comes as Oracle's cloud infrastructure business becomes more related to the AI expenditure boom.

Cloud infrastructure revenue rose 93% to $5.8 billion last quarter. Oracle also closed fiscal 2026 with $638 billion in remaining performance obligations, which is a substantial backlog of business already under contract. But there's a cost to such growth.

Oracle generated $32 billion in operating cash flow in fiscal 2026, but its free cash flow plunged to a negative $23.7 billion as the business spent heavily on AI data centers. That means Thursday's report is about more than whether Oracle beats quarterly projections.

The big concern for investors is whether the AI cloud income explosion can justify the huge capital spending behind it. Options traders are already betting the response may send the stock soaring or plunging.

title: Options Traders Are Betting Oracle Has Another Move Left
